fatal_errors: Replacing at most 30% of the single Hf component corresponds to only about 6 at.% V in the whole alloy and cannot credibly deliver the claimed 10% density reduction on mass-balance grounds; the approximate reduction in average atomic mass is only about 6% before accounting for volume changes.

The cited evidence shows that V-containing RHEAs can retain high-temperature strength, but it does not establish that V-for-Hf substitution in HfMoTaTiZr will preserve its room-temperature strength, ductility, phase stability, or 1000 °C strength.
The proposed tensile tests are not directly comparable to the primarily compression-derived baseline properties, so apparent changes could reflect loading mode rather than composition.
The falsification rule incorrectly rejects the composition-range hypothesis if any tested variant fails, even though success at one composition could support the stated claim.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested density–performance trade-off and proposes a controlled composition series with numerical mechanical thresholds. However, it does not reconstruct the target Cr-addition intervention, reticulated Laves-phase mediator, solid-solution hardening mechanism, or the observed simultaneous increases in compressive yield strength and fracture strain. More importantly, its central density prediction is quantitatively implausible for the specified substitution range. The evidence supports only the broad idea that lower-density refractory elements, including V, can be used in RHEAs; it does not validate preservation of HfMoTaTiZr's exceptional properties. Phase identification, lattice-parameter measurements, segregation analysis, and matched compression testing would be required for a discriminating test.
